pr_title: fix issue #9432(uses reference to loop iterator variable )
pr_comments:
Thanks! Do you mind adding a test for this? Something like two rules in a group, each with a syntax issue, and then check to make sure each error has unique information.

```yaml
groups:
- name: example
  rules:
  - alert: InstanceDown
    expr: up ===== 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: "page"
    annotations:
      summary: "Instance {{ $labels.instance }} down"
  - alert: InstanceUp
    expr: up == 1
    for: 5mmmmm
    labels:
      severity: "page"
    annotations:
      summary: "Instance {{ $labels.instance }} up"
```
And also please make sure to sign your commits.

issue_context.title: Report a coding issue that uses reference to loop iterator variable
issue_context.body:
**What did you do?**

Run a static analyzer DeepGo, which reports a finding on the related code.

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**

At https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go#L85-86,
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a7d499e19a932f4f7cf14e8b8c935dd43d2a9830/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go#L85-L86

Within the loop `for i, r := range g.Rules`, variable `r` is shared by all the loop iterations, as described in the Go specification (https://golang.org/ref/spec).
All instances of `&r` and its field addresses such as `&r.Record` within the loop may refer to the last rule updated by the loop. 
```
		for i, r := range g.Rules {
			for _, node := range r.Validate() {
```
Within `r.Validate()`, the return value `nodes` includes multiple instances of the same `&r.Record`:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a7d499e19a932f4f7cf14e8b8c935dd43d2a9830/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go#L135-L140

Next, all the nodes returned by `r.Validate()` are appended into the `errs` slice, which escapes the loop:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a7d499e19a932f4f7cf14e8b8c935dd43d2a9830/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go#L93-L97

As a consequence, `errs` may hold multiple instances of the same rule's fields.

For example, supposed `g.Rules = [r1, r2]`,  code
```
		for i, r := range g.Rules {
			for _, node := range r.Validate() {
				...
				errs = append(errs, &Error{
					Group:    g.Name,
					Rule:     i + 1,
					RuleName: ruleName.Value,
					Err:      node,
				})
			}
		}
```
produces
```
errs = [
  &Error{..., Err: WrappedError{ ..., node:  &r2.Record} },
  &Error{..., Err: WrappedError{ ..., node:  &r2.Record} },
]
```
That is, it contains two instances of `&r2.Record`, while the correct result should be:
```
errs = [
  &Error{..., Err: WrappedError{ ..., node:  &r1.Record} },
  &Error{..., Err: WrappedError{ ..., node:  &r2.Record} },
]
```

**What did you expect to see?**

A fix is to avoid reusing the shared variable item:
```
		for i, r := range g.Rules {
			for _, node := range g.Rules[i].Validate() {
				...
```

**Found by #deepgo.**
comments: Thanks for the report, nice catch!

review_comments: `TestReferenceToLoopIteratorVariable` is a little vague, how about something like `TestUniqueErrorNodes`?

We should check to make sure we have two errors before proceeding to extract the nodes.

```suggestion
		require.Len(t, errs, 2, "Expected two errors")
    	err0 := errs[0].(*Error).Err.node
		err1 := errs[1].(*Error).Err.node
```

It would be nice to have a descriptive error message here, as currently it will output something like "Expected false but got true."

```suggestion
		require.False(t, reflect.DeepEqual(err0, err1), "Error nodes should not be the same")
```
(or equivalent)

Because we only have and need one case, it's not necessary to set up a multi-case test.

```suggestion
  group := `
groups:
- name: example
  rules:
  - alert: InstanceDown
    expr: up ===== 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: "page"
    annotations:
      summary: "Instance {{ $labels.instance }} down"
  - alert: InstanceUp
    expr: up ===== 1
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: "page"
    annotations:
      summary: "Instance {{ $labels.instance }} up"
`,

	_, errs := Parse([]byte(group))
```
